supporting_observations.claim: The provided records documenting the large outbound transfer place it at 13:49:52 UTC, rather than around 13:46 UTC. The proxy reports 640,000,000 client-to-server bytes, and Zeek records 640,000,409 outbound bytes in the corresponding connection.

The transfer went to ingest.ironvault-cloud.com. The associated process was C:\Program Files\Ironvault\agent.exe, running as COPPERLINE\svc-backup with a Nightly job command targeting that same Ironvault host. The inventory identifies Ironvault as an approved backup service whose agent uploads several hundred MB.

Shortly before the agent ran, the domain controller recorded a service-ticket event for svc-backup from 91.219.236.174; a local service logon for svc-backup followed, then the Ironvault process started. The external source is anomalous given the provided environment context, which states there is no VPN.
The proxy records the transfer with user agent Wget/1.21.3, while endpoint network telemetry attributes the proxy connections to Ironvault agent.exe. The records do not explain this difference.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy and Zeek records establish destination and transfer volume, but the provided records do not expose the transferred files or their contents (T120-00307, T120-00309, T120-00311).

The records show an external source IP in a svc-backup service-ticket event and a subsequent local service logon, but do not establish who controlled that source or whether the ticket event caused the local logon or upload (T120-00298, T120-00299, T120-00305).
The provided evidence does not show the Ironvault job schedule or establish whether this Nightly upload was expected at this time (T120-00305, T120-00306).
claims_not_established: Whether the svc-backup authentication from 91.219.236.174 was authorized, spoofed, or evidence of credential compromise (T120-00298, T120-00299).
Whether the 640 MB upload contained only expected backup data or included unauthorized data (T120-00307, T120-00311).
Whether the Wget user-agent value reflects normal Ironvault behavior or a different execution path (T120-00307, T120-00314, T120-00315).
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate the 13:49:14 svc-backup ticket event with domain-controller authentication details, source-network ownership, and any relevant service-account authentication records.
Review Ironvault job history and audit records for the 13:49 Nightly run, including the backup set, file manifest, and destination-side receipt.
Verify the Ironvault agent binary and its execution provenance, and determine why the proxy logged a Wget user agent.
Check whether the alert's original network-flow telemetry independently confirms the transfer time and destination.
unrelated_findings: Separate ticket: sara.ali, identified in the inventory as help desk and not an administrator, initiated RDP to FILE-COP-01 and obtained an interactive logon. This is outside the alerted upload activity and should not determine this alert's disposition (T120-00422, T120-00427, T120-00434).
